capabilities.description: The project's complete new capabilities, replacing the current ones in the same publish. Send it when the change needs a capability the canvas does not declare yet, for example a new ph.state scope, insight, capture event, or network origin. Copy the current capabilities from canvas-source-retrieve and change only what you need. Omit to keep the current capabilities.

connectors.description: Third-party providers the canvas reads through ph.connectors, each with the tools it may call. Every call runs with the viewer's own connection; declaring one shows it in the promote review.

items.description: One provider a canvas may call through ph.connectors, with the tools it may use.

provider.description: Connector provider id: a native provider such as 'github', or 'mcp:<server host>' (e.g. 'mcp:mcp.calendly.com') for a server the viewer connected in the MCP store.

tools.description: Tool names the canvas may call on this provider. Read-only tools only.

actions.description: Registered action verbs the canvas may invoke via ph.actions (e.g. 'annotations.create', 'tasks.create'). Each executes as the viewer; declaring one shows it in the promote review.

data.description: The events, properties, and tables the canvas reads. A nightly check compares them with the project's current schema and flags drift on the canvas, from which a person requests a fix.

events.description: Event names the canvas's queries read.

properties.description: Properties the canvas's queries read or filter on.

items.description: One property a canvas reads, with the kind of property it is.

type.description:
Which kind of property the name refers to.

* `event` - event
* `person` - person
* `group` - group
* `session` - session

tables.description: Data warehouse table names the canvas's queries read.

operations.description: Named operations agents may invoke on this canvas, each bound to a declared verb. Listed by the operations endpoint and exported as a team skill.

items.description: One named operation a canvas exposes to agents: a verb with a fixed payload and the inputs a caller supplies.

description.description: What invoking the operation does for a person, in one or two sentences.

inputs.description: Payload fields the caller supplies at invoke time. Any other argument is refused.

name.description: Operation name: lowercase letters, digits, and single hyphens, e.g. 'enable-beta'.

payload.description: Fixed verb arguments the operation always sends, keyed by the verb's payload fields.

verb.description: Registered verb the operation runs; it must also be in capabilities.posthog.actions.

state.description: State scopes the canvas may use via ph.state: 'user' (private to each viewer) and/or 'shared' (one value per canvas, team-visible).

expected_current_version_id.description: Required optimistic-concurrency guard: the current_version_id the edits are based on (null when the canvas has never been published). Diff edits against a moved head are rejected with 409 version_conflict — they cannot be published unguarded.

id.description: ID of the canvas whose source to edit.

name.description: Optional new display name for the canvas.

operations.description: Edits applied in order to the canvas's current source project, all or nothing. May be empty when the edit only changes capabilities.

items.description: One file edit: replace text in a file, write a whole file, delete it, or rename it.

content.description: For 'write': the file's complete new content.

new_path.description: For 'rename': the file's new project-relative path.

new_string.description: For 'str_replace': the text that replaces old_string. An empty string deletes old_string.

old_string.description: For 'str_replace': the exact text to replace, copied from the file with a few surrounding lines so it matches one place only. If whitespace differs slightly, a unique line-by-line match is still accepted.

op.description:
What to do. 'str_replace' replaces old_string with new_string inside the file: the default for changing an existing file. 'write' sets the file's complete content (new files, full rewrites). 'delete' removes the file. 'rename' moves it to new_path. When omitted, it follows the fields sent: old_string or new_string means 'str_replace', new_path means 'rename', non-null content means 'write', and content null means 'delete'. An operation with none of these fields is rejected.

* `write` - Write
* `delete` - Delete
* `rename` - Rename
* `str_replace` - Str Replace

path.description: Project-relative path of the file to edit (e.g. "src/canvas.tsx").

replace_all.description: For 'str_replace': replace every exact match of old_string instead of requiring exactly one.

prompt.description: Short description of the change, stored on the appended version history entry.
